item.title: Pacific Governments urged to take journalists on overseas trips
item.description: Prime Ministers Department and other government agencies in the Pacific have been urged to involve mainstream media journalists in international engagements involving senior political leaders. NBC PNG Executive Director Provincial Radio [EDPR-NBC PNG] Rose Amos made the call during a panel discussion at the 8th Pacific Media Summit in Savusavu, Vanua Levu, Fiji.
item.content:encoded:
Prime Ministers Department and other government agencies in the Pacific have been urged to involve mainstream media journalists in international engagements involving senior political leaders.

NBC PNG Executive Director Provincial Radio [EDPR-NBC PNG] Rose Amos made the call during a panel discussion at the 8th Pacific Media Summit in Savusavu, Vanua Levu, Fiji.

Ms Amos says journalists should be given the opportunity to accompany prominent political leaders on international trips so they can independently report on the activities and provide checks and balances.

She also says newsrooms should not have to depend only on press releases prepared by public relations officers.

“We need our mainstream journalists to be there. We need to accompany our leaders so that we can ask the questions, we can see what is happening and we can provide that independent reporting to the public," Ms Amos says.

Amos stress press releases can be useful to journalists but should be treated as background information rather than the complete news story.

She furthers that public relations officers have a responsibility to communicate the position and activities of the organisations they represent, while journalists have a responsibility to serve the wider public.

“A press release is background information. It should not become the story itself. As journalists, we have to go out there, check the information, ask questions and find out what is really happening.”

She adds this is particularly important when reporting on government decisions, international meetings and activities involving prominent political figures.

Ms Amos says having journalists physically present also allows them to ask questions that may not be covered in an official statement.

“Our job is to provide checks and balances. We cannot just rely on what the PR officer gives us because our responsibility is to the public.”

" I understand there are budgets allocated for media for in the organisation or government departments and journalists must be captured in that to accompany especially the PMs and its delegations to events in the international arena or domestic so that journalists can provide back to the people/public the information they need to know," Amos stressed.

The comments received wider support from media leaders and journalists attending the summit, with the discussion focusing on the need for independent reporting and stronger accountability.

The call comes as Pacific media organisations examine press freedom, media sustainability, digital innovation and the changing role of journalism.

The summit has also emphasised the importance of journalists questioning, investigating and holding institutions accountable.

For PNG newsrooms, the discussion highlights the importance of direct access to decision-makers, particularly when major government activities are carried out overseas.

It also places a greater responsibility on journalists to go beyond official statements by asking questions, checking facts, seeking other perspectives and reporting what they independently observe.

item.title: Lae AFL semi-finals set for weekend
item.description: The 2026 Lae AFL Senior Men's competition moves into the semi-finals this weekend, with teams fighting for a place in the grand final. The semi-finals will be played on Saturday, September 26, and Sunday, September 27, at Eriku Oval.
item.content:encoded:
The 2026 Lae AFL Senior Men's competition moves into the semi-finals this weekend, with teams fighting for a place in the grand final.

The semi-finals will be played on Saturday, September 26, and Sunday, September 27, at Eriku Oval.

Eight teams took part in this year's competition, with clubs fielding squads of up to 30 players.

Lae AFL President Alang Issac says the introduction of 10 new sets of jerseys has been one of the highlights of the season.

He says the competition has also focused on bringing clubs, officials, coaches and players together.

The grand final is set for Sunday, October 4, at Eriku Oval, with free entry for spectators.

The competition also had three women's teams this season, with the Equal Footing program expected to expand next year.

Issac says Lae AFL wants to see more young players develop their skills and eventually become leaders and ambassadors for the sport.

The focus now turns to this weekend's semi-finals, with the winners securing their place in the October 4 grand final.

item.title: Communities mourn journalist Samson Bonai
item.description: Communities in Bulolo and Wau Waria have lost a familiar voice following the death of veteran journalist Samson Bonai, who spent much of his working life reporting on the people and issues of Morobe Province. Although originally from East Sepik, Bonai built his journalism career in Morobe, where he covered communities, development projects and issues affecting people in some of the province’s more
item.content:encoded:
Communities in Bulolo and Wau Waria have lost a familiar voice following the death of veteran journalist Samson Bonai, who spent much of his working life reporting on the people and issues of Morobe Province.

Although originally from East Sepik, Bonai built his journalism career in Morobe, where he covered communities, development projects and issues affecting people in some of the province’s more remote areas.

For the communities he reported from, his work meant their stories could reach audiences beyond their villages and districts.

His death last week has prompted reflection on the role he played in bringing local concerns, development needs and community achievements into the public eye.

Wau Waria MP Marsh Narewec said Bonai’s work was particularly important to the new district, which still needed greater visibility among government agencies, donors and development partners.

Narewec said journalists helped connect communities with decision-makers by reporting what was happening on the ground.

“We are a new district, and many people, government agencies, donors and development partners may not yet know about our existence or the work we are doing,” he said.

He said Bonai and other journalists helped change that by reporting on development projects and the experiences of local communities.

Narewec also urged the media to continue reporting problems, saying critical coverage could help leaders identify areas requiring attention.

“We should not be worried when the media publishes bad stories about us. Those stories can help guide us,” he said.

For the communities Bonai covered, his passing means losing a journalist who spent years documenting their lives, challenges and hopes through his work.

item.title: Womai tribe calls for justice over Dr Waiye’s death
item.description: Relatives and tribesmen of the late Dr Robert Waiye have staged a peaceful march in Kundiawa, Simbu Province, calling for justice over his death. Members of the Tabare Local Level Government, Tunaku Tribe and Womai Village in the Sinasina-Yongomugl District walked about three kilometres from Womai Village to Kundiawa town today, Wednesday, September 23.
item.content:encoded:
Relatives and tribesmen of the late Dr Robert Waiye have staged a peaceful march in Kundiawa, Simbu Province, calling for justice over his death.

Members of the Tabare Local Level Government, Tunaku Tribe and Womai Village in the Sinasina-Yongomugl District walked about three kilometres from Womai Village to Kundiawa town today, Wednesday, September 23.

They carried banners calling for “Justice for Dr Robert Waiye” before presenting a petition to provincial authorities.

Presenting the petition, Rev John Kamane, Chairman of the Simbu Education Board and an uncle of the late Dr Waiye, said the family and tribe did not want mediation or compensation.

“No mediation and no compensation, but the full force of the law. The amount of compensation will not add up to what we have lost, and therefore we want full justice to be served,” Rev. Kamane said.

He said the tribe was also calling on the Government to consider the death penalty for those found responsible for Dr Waiye’s death.

Rev Kamane called on Sinasina-Yongomugl MP Kerenga Kua to table the petition in Parliament.

The petition was presented to the Simbu Provincial Government, provincial administration, police, Simbu Provincial Health Authority and the province’s six Members of Parliament.

Deputy Governor Billy Siwi, representing Governor Noah Kool and the Simbu Provincial Government, accepted the petition and assured the group that the provincial government would assist in seeking justice.

He also apologised to the Tabare people, Womai Village, the district and the family of Dr Waiye over his death.

“Simbu is saddened that one of our doctors has fallen. SPG will stand behind to make sure justice prevails,” Mr Siwi said.

Eastern End Command and Assistant Police Commissioner Chief Superintendent Clement Dalla thanked the people of Tabare and Sinasina-Yongomugl for conducting the march peacefully.

He confirmed that seven people are in police custody in connection with Dr Waiye’s death and assured the group that the matter would be dealt with through the law.

Sinasina-Yongomugl MP Kerenga Kua, Provincial Administrator John Punde, police personnel, SiPHA representatives and other provincial leaders and community members attended the petition presentation.

Police investigations into Dr Waiye’s death are continuing.

item.title: PNG PMs XIII squad named
item.description: The Papua New Guinea Prime Minister’s XIII Women’s squad has been named ahead of the official kick-off at the Santos National Football Stadium next Saturday. The 20-player squad brings together leading players from the recently concluded Santos Cup, along with PNG players currently based overseas.
item.content:encoded:
The Papua New Guinea Prime Minister’s XIII Women’s squad has been named ahead of the official kick-off at the Santos National Football Stadium next Saturday.

The 20-player squad brings together leading players from the recently concluded Santos Cup, along with PNG players currently based overseas.

The match will give established players and emerging talent the opportunity to test themselves against Australia.

Former Wallaroos XVs capped player Ivania Wong is set to wear the PNG colours for the first time after being named in the PM’s XIII Women’s squad.

The East New Britain-born player currently plays for the ACT Brumbies in the Super Rugby Women’s competition.

Other notable players include dual-code representatives and former PNG Palais 7s players Alice Alois and Cynthia Peters, who both featured in the recent Santos Cup.

Anika Butler and Gemma Schnaubelt are among the players based overseas.

The side will be coached by Cathy Neap, who brings extensive coaching experience after guiding the Central Dabaris to back-to-back Santos Cup premierships in 2025 and 2026.

Neap has coached the Dabaris since the Santos Cup was introduced in 2024 and will now take on the opportunity to lead the Prime Minister’s XIII Women against Australia.

Neap said the opportunity to represent PNG in front of a home crowd would be an important moment for the players and called on them to embrace the occasion and play for one another.

“I would like to congratulate every player selected in the Prime Minister’s XIII Women’s squad. Each of these players has worked hard to reach this level, and now they have a wonderful opportunity to represent Papua New Guinea in front of their home supporters.

“I want the girls to believe in themselves, play for one another and show the commitment and determination they have demonstrated throughout their careers.

“We are grateful to PNGRFL for giving us this opportunity and for continuing to invest in the growth of women’s rugby league in PNG,” she added.

The PNG PM’s XIII Women will face Australia’s PM’s XIII Women, with kick-off scheduled for 12:15pm local time.

item.title: Researchers challenged to turn knowledge into innovation
item.description: Researchers have been challenged to connect local knowledge with science and technology to develop innovations that can have a meaningful impact on Papua New Guinea. The challenge was made during the opening of the 8th Papua New Guinea Science and Technology Conference in Goroka, Eastern Highlands Province.
item.content:encoded:
Researchers have been challenged to connect local knowledge with science and technology to develop innovations that can have a meaningful impact on Papua New Guinea.

The challenge was made during the opening of the 8th Papua New Guinea Science and Technology Conference in Goroka, Eastern Highlands Province.

Themed “Refocusing Science, Technology and Innovation for Inclusive Growth, Resilience and Prosperity for the Future,” the three-day conference brings together scientists, academics, researchers, students and development partners.

Participants are sharing ideas, research and innovations, while looking at ways to connect local knowledge with science and technology to address challenges facing the country.

Minister for Higher Education, Research, Science and Technology and Unggai-Bena MP Kinoka Feo delivered his opening address via Zoom from China, highlighting the role of technology in shaping PNG’s future.

“What kind of future do we want science, research, and technology to help build for PNG?” Minister Feo asked

He said science, research and technology should be measured by their ability to improve people’s lives, strengthen institutions, create opportunities, protect the environment and respond to national challenges.

As he formally declared the conference open, Minister Feo challenged researchers to apply emerging technologies to present-day realities and develop innovations that can influence government policy and provide practical solutions for communities.

The conference is funded by the PNG Science and Technology Council Secretariat and hosted by the University of Goroka in partnership with the PNG Institute of Medical Research.

item.title: Immigration Minister warns foreigners over human trafficking
item.description: Immigration and Border Security Minister William Bando has warned foreigners in Papua New Guinea to respect the country’s laws, following the discovery of an alleged human trafficking operation in Port Moresby. The warning comes after police rescued 39 Indonesian nationals who were allegedly being held against their will at a residential property in downtown Port Moresby on Tuesday.
item.content:encoded:
Immigration and Border Security Minister William Bando has warned foreigners in Papua New Guinea to respect the country’s laws, following the discovery of an alleged human trafficking operation in Port Moresby.

The warning comes after police rescued 39 Indonesian nationals who were allegedly being held against their will at a residential property in downtown Port Moresby on Tuesday.

Four Chinese nationals have been detained as police investigate the alleged trafficking and people-smuggling operation.

Minister Bando said he was concerned about the incident and would establish a special investigation task force to investigate the alleged network and those involved.

He said the trafficking of people, including concealing them in residential areas and exploiting them for cheap labour or other criminal activities, was a serious concern.

Bando warned that foreigners found to be connected to trafficking networks or involved in facilitating such activities could face visa cancellation, deportation and bans from entering Papua New Guinea.

He said the country must not become a transit point for transnational criminal activities in the region.

The Minister also claimed he had received intelligence reports about various illegal activities allegedly involving organised criminal groups, including human trafficking, illegal logging, illegal alluvial mining, money laundering and the use of state agencies to facilitate such activities.

He warned foreigners who are investing or working in Papua New Guinea to respect the country’s laws.

“Failure to do so will result in detention, prosecution and removal,” he said.

Bando also warned Papua New Guineans, including public servants in immigration, customs and police, against becoming involved in such activities.

He said those found to be involved would face criminal prosecution.

The Minister acknowledged weaknesses in the country’s border and immigration systems, saying these vulnerabilities could be exploited by criminal networks.

He said the Government would focus on strengthening national security measures, including border control and immigration policies, as well as tougher penalties for people in positions of trust who conspire to facilitate criminal activities.

Bando also said he would push for a national migration policy and a comprehensive review of the Immigration Act 1978 to address gaps and strengthen the protection of PNG’s borders.

item.title: Central passes K364.9 million supplementary budget
item.description: The Central Provincial Government has passed a K364.9 million supplementary budget for the 2026 fiscal year. The revised appropriation increases the province’s budget by K19.6 million, from the original K345.3 million to K364.9 million.
item.content:encoded:
The Central Provincial Government has passed a K364.9 million supplementary budget for the 2026 fiscal year.

The revised appropriation increases the province’s budget by K19.6 million, from the original K345.3 million to K364.9 million.

The supplementary budget was passed on Tuesday following the recent National Government supplementary budget, which undertook significant reprioritization in response to fuel price pressures, the El Niño response, preparations for the 2027 National General Election and additional security requirements.

Central Governor and Chairperson for Finance and Planning Rufina Peter, while presenting the revised budget, said the supplementary budget would respond to the province’s immediate fiscal position and begin repositioning the province towards a stronger and more sustainable financial base.

“The supplementary budget therefore will do two things, firstly respond to the immediate 2026 fiscal position and secondly begins repositioning the province towards a stronger and more sustainable fiscal base,” Governor Peter said.

The revised budget includes provisions for PNG LNG royalties, PNG LNG development levies, El Niño response, infrastructure grants, Provincial Assembly maintenance and the Papua LNG development forum process.

Governor Peter said the supplementary budget must also serve as a bridge into the province’s 2027 budget, linking the immediate fiscal requirements with the province’s longer-term development priorities.

The passage of the supplementary budget gives the Central Provincial Government a revised financial framework to manage its remaining 2026 commitments while preparing its priorities and fiscal position for the 2027 financial year.
